title: A mighty fortress

lines: A VERY PRESENT HELP IN TROUBLE.
EIN FESTE BURG IST UNSER GOTT.
cards: "God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble." That's how Psalm 46 opens in the King James Bible. Then look what it does next.
The earth moves. The mountains slide into the sea. The waters roar.

By its second verse the psalm is standing in the middle of the shaking, and it says, right there, we will not fear. Martin Luther turned this psalm into a hymn. In his German it opens Ein feste Burg ist unser Gott.
In English it's often sung as a mighty fortress is our God.

teach.b: The psalm is short and strange. Its second verse, in the King James wording: "Therefore will not we fear, though the earth be removed." Not because nothing bad is happening.
Because God is a refuge while it happens.

teach.h: A RIVER IN THE CITY OF GOD.
teach.b: Then, in the middle of all that roaring water, a different water appears: "There is a river, the streams whereof shall make glad the city of God." Floods outside, a gentle river inside the city.

teach.h: BE STILL, IN THE MIDDLE OF A WAR.
teach.b: And near the end, after bows broken and spears cut in two, comes this: "Be still, and know that I am God." It comes right after talk of war, not at a spa.

teach.h: LUTHER BUILDS IT INTO A FORTRESS.
teach.b: Luther took the psalm's refuge and made it a castle, a fortress with walls. His verses name an old enemy, the devil, scheming and armed.
They admit human strength won't win that fight, and they name the one who fights for us: Christ. A single little word, the hymn says, can bring the enemy down. The last verse is the bravest.
In paraphrase: let them take our goods, our honor, even our families and our lives; they gain nothing, and the kingdom still stands.

So one psalm gives two pictures: a fortress to shelter in when the enemy comes, and a river and a stillness in the middle of the city. Some Christians lean on the walls, some on the stillness. The psalm holds both.

how: Lutheran churches sing "A Mighty Fortress Is Our God," and other churches sing it too; Psalm 46 is read in worship and in private prayer.

games.q: you're turning Psalm 46 into a song for people who feel the world shaking. which picture do you build it on?
o: the quiet river in the city.
games.why: Luther built his hymn on the fortress: God as a stronghold against an old enemy. the river and the stillness stay in the psalm for anyone who reads it.

practice: Read Psalm 46 slowly, out loud if you can; it's short, and it's in any Bible or on your phone.
If reading isn't possible right now, hold its three pictures instead: mountains sliding into the sea, a river running quietly through a city, and the words be still.
If you pray, let the first verse be your prayer; if you don't, sit with whichever picture keeps coming back.
